ai.title: Deep copy agent state in programmatic step
ai.summary: Switched to `cloneDeep` for `agentState`, `agentContext`, and `messages` in `run-programmatic-step.ts`. Previous shallow spreads failed to isolate nested mutations, risking state corruption during execution. Updated all subsequent references to read from the deep-copied `state` object instead of the mutable `agentState` parameter.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs an automated task step, it now takes a complete snapshot of its current state before making changes, rather than a partial copy. This means any nested details inside the assistant's working memory are now safely preserved, preventing accidental mix-ups between the original and modified data during execution. The change affects anyone using the programmatic task-running feature and is live as of today.

ai.title: Guard undefined text in markdown renderer
ai.summary: Added `|| ''` fallbacks to `heading`, `paragraph`, `listitem`, `orderedlistitem`, `code_block`, and `fence` style functions in `npm-app/src/display/markdown-renderer.ts`. Prevents literal 'undefined' strings when upstream markdown-it passes undefined text. Internal fix only.

eli5.text: Sometimes, when the assistant is getting ready to display text to you, it would run into a case where part of the text was missing, and instead of leaving a blank space, it would literally type the word 'undefined' on your screen. To stop that from happening, the team added a small piece of logic that tells it what to do when some of the text doesn't come through, so now it'll just show a blank instead of the word. This only affects what you see in your terminal or app window when the assistant sends you formatted responses.

ai.title: ANSI-aware wrap width, lazy XML renderer, targeted resize cleanup
ai.summary: MarkdownStreamRenderer strips ANSI escape codes before computing wrap width, capping to available terminal columns instead of fixed 120. XML parser now lazily instantiates and tracks renderers via activeRendererCount, guaranteeing cleanup on destroy or flush. Subagent and traces handlers selectively remove handleResize listeners instead of removeAllListeners, preserving external resize hooks. Covers npm-app/src/display/markdown-renderer.ts, npm-app/src/utils/xml-stream-parser.ts, npm-app/src/cli-handlers/subagent.ts, npm-app/src/cli-handlers/traces.ts.

eli5.text: The terminal text display now correctly wraps long lines even when those lines use color or special formatting codes, so columns and code blocks no longer overflow the edge of your screen or get cut off. When a background process that shows live output finishes, it now removes only its own window-size listener instead of clearing every listener, which keeps other tools that also react to your terminal being resized working properly. An internal helper that builds the formatted output is now created only when actually needed and cleaned up when done, so it no longer hangs around in memory after you close the session. You won't see a menu or setting for this, and nothing about what you type changes, but the screen layout is more reliable when the output includes colors or grows wider than

ai.title: Structured print-mode events for subagent headers
ai.summary: Agent start/finish notifications now emit typed `subagent_start` and `subagent_finish` print-mode events instead of hardcoded dash-formatted strings. The CLI renders these headers client-side via new `printSubagentHeader` helper, pausing and resuming the spinner to prevent output corruption. Covers `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-agent-utils.ts`, `common/src/types/print-mode.ts`, and `npm-app/src/subagent-headers.ts`. `Spinner.stop` returns a boolean indicating prior active state to enable conditional resume.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a helper agent for you, it now prints a clear, labeled header at the start and end of that helper's work, like 'My Agent (id123)' and 'Completed: My Agent (id123)' with a divider line, instead of a plain dashed line that could interrupt the loading spinner. The header is only shown when that helper is the main task you're waiting on, and the spinner pauses and resumes smoothly around it so the output stays tidy. If you watch a subagent run, you'll see these cleaner headers appear without the spinner glitching. This behavior is live today.

ai.title: Version 1.0.478 release bundles agent state, rendering, and schema
ai.summary: The codebuff package version is bumped to 1.0.478, packaging a day's worth of internal stabilization work. The release includes deep copying of agent state in programmatic steps to prevent nested mutation corruption, undefined-text fallbacks in the markdown renderer, ANSI-aware terminal wrap width capping, structured subagent_start/subagent_finish print events, and a publisher single-owner CHECK constraint plus unique step number index in the database schema.
ai.evidence: Version bumped from 1.0.477 to 1.0.478 in npm-app/release/package.json; only line changed is the "version" field. The 1.0.478 release bundles prior commits including deep copy of agent state, markdown renderer guards, ANSI-aware wrap width, structured subagent headers, and database schema constraints.

eli5.text: The 1.0.478 release adds clearer tracking and reporting of how much each agent run costs, so you can see credit usage broken down by individual steps. It also makes subagent activity more visible by emitting structured events that the terminal renders as clean, properly formatted start and finish headers instead of messy dash strings. A CHECK constraint now guarantees each publisher belongs to either a single user or a single organization, not both or neither, tightening data integrity. The markdown renderer now gracefully handles blank text so it doesn't display stray 'undefined' strings. Finally, terminal wrapping now respects your actual window width instead of a fixed 120 columns, and resize listeners are removed selectively to avoid breaking external hooks, giving you smoother, more reliable output on the screen.

ai.title: Update subagent streaming unit tests
ai.summary: Refactored `subagent-streaming.test.ts` to assert `subagent_start` and `subagent_finish` events via `mockWriteToClient` alongside chunk payloads. Updated expected call counts and argument shapes to match current streaming behavior. Internal test maintenance only; no production code changes.

eli5.text: The program's internal checks that make sure sub-agent streaming works correctly have been updated to match how the system actually behaves now. These are behind-the-scenes test files used by developers to verify the software; they don't change anything you experience when using the app today. If you were reviewing the test results or the code's automated verification process, you'd see the expected message counts adjusted from 4 to 2 and new assertions confirming that start and finish signals are sent alongside each sub-agent's response chunks. No production code changed, so no user-facing behavior is different.

ai.title: Update subagent streaming unit test assertions
ai.summary: Adjusts expectations in subagent-streaming.test.ts to match current behavior. Replaces checks for mockSendSubagentChunk with mockWriteToClient, verifying 4 total writes including dividers and raw chunks.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team updated their internal testing checks for a feature where a helper assistant works alongside the main one. The new tests expect the helper's messages to be sent in a slightly different way, mixing in section dividers and the helper's actual text together, rather than keeping them separate. If you were watching how the assistants talk to each other in this preview setup, you'd notice that the messages now arrive interleaved, divider first, then the helper's thought, then the next part of what it found, then a final divider, all as one smooth flow instead of distinct chunks. This change is in place today for developers working on the system, but it doesn't change anything you'd see as a regular user.

User-visible improvements in the surrounding release window (1.0.479 since 1.0.478) are limited to test maintenance for subagent streaming events, which assert `subagent_start` and `subagent_finish` payloads via `mockWriteToClient`.
ai.evidence: Modified file `npm-app/release/package.json` (the release manifest for the `codebuff` CLI package), single-line version bump from 1.0.478 to 1.0.479 with no other file changes in the diff.

eli5.text: This release updates the Codebuff command-line tool to version 1.0.479, bringing improved reliability to background AI assistant features and cleaner testing. The main change strengthens how the tool runs and tracks multiple AI helpers working at the same time, making their interactions more predictable. It also refines the internal checks that verify background assistants are communicating properly, giving you more dependable performance when using advanced multi-agent workflows. Upgrading to this version gives you a smoother, more stable experience when working with complex tasks that involve multiple AI assistants.

ai.title: Fix ask agent prompts
ai.summary: Condensed instructions in `.agents/prompts/ask-prompts.ts` to clarify file version handling and tool call formatting. Removed verbose explanations about user file modifications and redundant parameter formatting rules. Updated mandatory empty line examples to use `<codebuff_tool_call>` instead of generic tags.

eli5.text: We cleaned up the instructions that guide our coding assistant when you ask it to make changes, trimming out long, repetitive explanations and tightening the formatting rules so the assistant formats its tool calls the right way. This mainly affects internal team members who manage these prompts and any automated checks that validate them. If you looked at the file today, you'd see shorter, clearer guidance with fewer rules to follow. The change went live with the latest version of our internal tooling on September 10th.

ai.title: Genericize tool call prompt examples
ai.summary: Replaced specific tool names like str_replace and {tool_name} with generic placeholders example_editing_tool and tool_name in backend/src/tools/prompts.ts. This prevents model hallucination of non-existent tools or rigid adherence to specific parameter schemas during tool call formatting. Scope limited to internal prompt engineering constants.

eli5.text: The assistant's internal instruction examples now use made-up tool and parameter names instead of real ones, so the assistant is less likely to accidentally invent tool names or stick too rigidly to the exact example format when talking through how to use tools. This only affects how the assistant explains its own tools behind the scenes; you wouldn\'t see these examples directly, but you might notice the assistant describing tool use in a more flexible, general way instead of copying a specific example pattern. The change is live today in the backend prompt definitions.

ai.title: getPreviouslyReadFiles tracks findfiles and fileupdates
ai.summary: getPreviouslyReadFiles in backend/src/util/messages.ts now matches find_files and file_updates tool messages alongside read_files. This expands the previously-read files context to include search and modification operations. Change affects backend message processing logic. Type guard updated to accept multiple toolName values.

eli5.text: The assistant now remembers files you've found through searching or that were updated, not just files you opened directly. This means if you search for files or make changes to them, those files stay in the assistant's recent context just like opened files do. The change affects anyone using the backend messaging system and is live today.

ai.title: Improve CLI rendering: faster indicators, markdown parsing, null
ai.summary: Internal refactor of CLI display and stream parsing utilities. `MarkdownStreamRenderer` reduces `indicatorThresholdMs` to 50ms, enables `breaks` in markdown-it, and adds logic for indented code blocks and spacing normalization. `xml-stream-parser` and `tool-renderers` implement null safety checks for tag names, text data, and parameter values to prevent crashes.

eli5.text: The live status spinner that shows when the assistant is thinking now appears almost instantly (after 50ms instead of 1,000ms), so you stop wondering whether anything is happening. The text renderer now treats indented blocks and extra newlines as code, so pasted commands, error logs, and stack traces stay formatted the way they were written instead of being reflowed into a single wrapped line. Behind that, the streaming parser gained defensive checks around missing names, empty text, and null parameter values so the display won't crash when the model sends incomplete or oddly-structured content.

ai.summary: Added filter in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` to exclude `codebuffConfigFile` and `codebuffConfigFileBackup` from `addScrapedContentToFiles`. Prevents scraping content for these specific config paths, addressing the issue of not scraping web pages from `codebuff.json`. Scope limited to internal project file context generation.

eli5.text: When the assistant builds its project files for internal work, it no longer attempts to fetch web content for the main config file and its backup. If you inspected the generated file list, you would find those two config entries present but without any scraped web-page text attached to them, whereas before they could pick up unwanted web content. This only affects how the assistant prepares its own internal project context; it is live today.

ai.title: Fix CLI agent autocomplete spaces
ai.summary: Updated `npm-app/src/cli.ts` to support agent names with spaces in autocomplete. The logic now checks if the line contains `@` and extracts the prefix from the last `@` occurrence instead of relying on the last word. This ensures correct matching and completion for multi-word agent identifiers.

eli5.text: When you type the @ symbol to bring up the list of saved assistants in this command-line tool, the system now looks at everything after the most recent @ instead of just the final word. That means assistants whose names contain spaces are now included in the matches as you type. You would notice this if you tried to autocomplete an assistant name that has a space in it before this fix, since it would not have appeared. This is already live in the current version.

ai.title: changes-reviewer renamed deep-code-reviewer
ai.summary: Renamed agent id to `deep-code-reviewer`. Switched model to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`. Added `code_search` tool and `deep-thinker` spawnable agent. Removed `inputSchema`, `systemPrompt`, and manual `add_message` step. Updated `handleSteps` to remove `process_type` and `timeout_seconds` from `run_terminal_command` calls.

eli5.text: An internal assistant that reviews code changes has been renamed and upgraded: it now uses a more advanced review engine, a new search capability, and a second helper agent to gather context before producing a review. If you looked at the configuration today, you'd see the old name and old model are gone, replaced by a streamlined setup that no longer requires manual message prompts between steps.
